finding: The serialized browser bridge incurred request/header and separate body-completion scheduling delays during rendering. Delivering parsed JSON from one asynchronous XMLHttpRequest completion improves the same Intel playback workload without caching state or changing CAS/filter semantics.

resource_timing_control.method: Nearest matching Resource Timing start within 2 ms; only unambiguous matches. Includes browser transport/interception, not just engine execution.

rejected_leads: TCP_NODELAY did not clear pacing, including with request interception removed. No server socket policy was changed.
Suppressing tooltip observer annotation did not clear pacing. No tooltip behavior was changed.
Removing interception alone produced inconsistent pacing and exposed a separate pause write. Maintained routing/offline protection remains intact.
product_changes: Browser-only invoke transport delivers and parses the full JSON body in one completion event. Same POST endpoint, authorization, payload, structured errors and fresh state/CAS pipeline. Native Tauri dispatch stays on its existing path.
Full-range pause skips the redundant filter write. Each playback session initializes its own window before its first frame.
Full-range request assertion waits for filterIdle before stopping request observation.
Six unit regressions cover authenticated payload/body completion, structured conflict/auth errors, malformed JSON, network/abort failures, missing token, and native dispatch/error isolation.
